subject: Tokens/sec validation plan for Dedicated capacity + measurement checkpoints
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan@vertexanalytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vertexanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — tokens/sec, latency, and measurement ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the performance looked promising. Before we move to a purchase commitment we need a concrete measurement plan and firmness on throughput guarantees for Dedicated. Specifically:

- How do you define tokens/sec and requests/sec for the Dedicated GPU pool (per-pool vs per-model)?
- What latency targets will you guarantee (p50/p95/p99) for generate endpoints with our expected seq lengths (prompt ~120 tokens, response avg ~180 tokens)?
- How will you measure those guarantees (test harness, tooling, warm-cache vs cold-cache windows)?
- What remedies/credits apply if targets are missed and how are they calculated?

We are also evaluating discount levels tied to committed capacity. To make an approval case internally we need an explicit test plan, the assumed GPU sizing for X tokens/sec, and proposed discount bands for 12- and 18-month commits.

Can you send a draft measurement/validation plan and a proposal for commit sizes (and assumptions) early next week? Procurement is on cc.

Best,
Megan
CTO, Vertex Analytics


From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan@vertexanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@vertexanalytics.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — tokens/sec, latency, and measurement ask

Hi Megan — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a draft throughput validation plan and supporting samples (throughput-test-plan.pdf, kv-latency-samples.csv). High level summary below; full details are in the attachment.

Summary of our proposed measurement and SLA approach:

1) Metric definitions
   - Tokens/sec (aggregate): sustained token-generation rate observed from the customer’s routed Dedicated pool, measured at the Redwood edge in tokens/s over a 1-minute sampling interval and averaged across the measurement window.
   - Requests/sec: completed generate requests/sec observed after any admission control (successful 2xx responses).
   - Latency: reported as p50/p95/p99 for model generate APIs measured from request acceptance at Redwood to final token flush. We report both payload and end-to-end RTT.

2) Measurement windows and baselines
   - Calibration window: 72-hour soak run using a blended mix of synthetic traces + 7-days-of-customer-sampled traces (we’ll sanitize).
   - Acceptance window: 30-calendar-day rolling window for SLA validation; for initial commit we require an initial 14-day acceptance run after provisioning.
   - Warm-cache vs cold-cache: we provide both views. SLA applies to warm-cache steady-state; we publish cold-cache profiles for capacity planning and will exclude first 5 minutes after pool restarts from SLA calculations.

3) Test harness and signal collection
   - We’ll run our standard throughput harness (attached) that replays request distributions and sequence-length histograms you confirm. Telemetry captured: tokens emitted, request success/failure, p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.

4) Acceptance criteria and breach handling
   - Acceptance: 95th-percentile tokens/sec >= committed target for 72-hour soak AND p99 latency <= agreed threshold (see SLA matrix attached).
   - Breach: we calculate SLA credits as percentage of monthly committed fee proportional to under-delivery (shortfall_tokens / committed_tokens) capped at 100% of monthly committed payment.
   - Immediate remedies: automatic routing to burst capacity (if available) and model variant fallback (quantized variant) while we resolve the root cause. Repeated breaches trigger an operational review and the credit formula above.

5) GPU sizing assumptions and example mapping
   - Example (baseline): A100 80GB equivalent - approximate sustained tokens/sec per GPU: 60k tokens/s for avg response length 180 tokens (conservative), up to 110k tokens/s for short responses (<=64 tokens). These are workload-dependent — we include an empiric per-model profile in the attachment.
   - Pool sizing formula: required_gpus = ceil(committed_tokens_per_sec / effective_tokens_per_gpu_adjusted_for_cache_and_overhead) with a recommended 10% buffer.

6) Discount bands (proposal)
   - 6 months / 250k tps sustained -> 15% list discount on committed portion.
   - 12 months / 400k tps sustained -> 22% list discount + 10% extra for auto-scaling burst credits.
   - 18 months / 500k tps sustained -> 28% list discount + dedicated pre-warmed pool and quarterly performance reviews.

Attachments: throughput-test-plan.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); kv-latency-samples.csv (CSV, 12KB) — see drive link included.

If that structure works I can convert this into a short SLA matrix and a DocuSign-ready exhibit for signatures. Would you like us to assume a 10% cache hit rate (conservative) or use your sample traces for sizing?

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Megan Ortiz <megan@vertexanalytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vertexanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — tokens/sec, latency, and measurement ask

Thanks Olga — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying items before we schedule acceptance testing:

- If we commit 18 months and target sustained 500k tokens/sec, can you move the discount to 30%?
- What exact GPU count and instance type do you assume for the 500k tps example? We need that for our infra team to clear the budget.
- Can legal/ procurement start the agreement in parallel? We’ll need the DocuSign exhibit as soon as possible.

Procurement is cc’d — they’ll follow up on PO and timing.

Best,
Megan

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Vertex pricing ask — compute assumptions and discount flexibility

Marcus / Lauren — quick internal note before I respond to Megan:

1) GPU assumptions for 500k tps
   - We should propose a conservative plan: 25 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (effective 20k tokens/s per GPU after accounting for average 180-token responses, KV cache hit rate 10%, and 10% overhead for routing + autoscaling headroom). That nets 25 * 20k = 500k tokens/s sustained.

2) Discount posture
   - 28% is our standard top-tier for 18 months in SLA-heavy deals. We can flex to 30% if: Vertex signs a 2x committed GPU prepayment or agrees to a 90-day non-cancel warranty clause. Otherwise keep 28% and offer a one-time onboarding credit.

3) Acceptance test mechanics
   - Run a 72-hour soak inside their VPC routing to our Dedicated pool, with sampling telemetry forwarded to their monitoring endpoint. Acceptance criteria: 95th percentile tokens/sec >= committed target AND p99 latency <= 650ms for their prompt/response mix. If p99 misses but 95th tokens/sec holds, we offer a partial credit and a remediation window (14 days) to fix infra/config.

4) Billing and credits calculation
   - Recommend we calculate monthly credit as: min( committed_fee_monthly, (committed_tokens - delivered_tokens)/committed_tokens * committed_fee_monthly ). Avoid complex multipliers; keep formula transparent.

Please confirm whether legal is comfortable with the 90-day warranty ask — if not we will offer the 30% only with prepayment. I will draft the DocuSign exhibit tying the SLA to the commit tiers and the acceptance test.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan@vertexanalytics.com>, procurement@vertexanalytics.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Final proposal: SLA matrix, measurement plan, and next steps for Vertex Dedicated commit

Hi Megan / procurement — following our internal review we’ve put together a concise SLA matrix and an updated test plan (attached: SLA-matrix-vertex.xlsx, throughput-test-plan.pdf). Key points below:

- Committed tiers and discounts
   - 6 months / 250k tps -> 15% discount on committed portion
   - 12 months / 400k tps -> 22% discount + quarterly perf reviews
   - 18 months / 500k tps -> 28% discount + option to move to 30% if Vertex agrees to either (a) 2x prepayment of committed GPU-hours OR (b) a 90-day non-cancel warranty on the committed portion.

- GPU sizing assumption (for 500k tps)
   - Proposed: 25 x A100-80GB-equivalent. Effective tokens/s per GPU = 20k (adjusted for seq length, 10% cache hit, and overhead). We will supply an empirical per-model profile as part of onboarding.

- Acceptance / measurement plan
   - Initial calibration: 72-hour soak run (customer traces + synthetic).
   - Acceptance window: 14-day initial acceptance followed by 30-day rolling SLA reporting.
   - Telemetry: tokens/s (1-min sampling), requests/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, KV cache hit.

- Breach handling and credits
   - Credits calculated monthly proportional to under-delivery: shortfall_tokens/committed_tokens * monthly_committed_fee.
   - Immediate operational mitigations: automatic burst routing (if enabled) + model variant fallback while we remediate.

Next steps
   - I will upload the DocuSign exhibit linking the SLA matrix to the Master Services Agreement: https://app.docusign.com/agreements/0A1B2C3D4E
   - Proposed timeline: schedule calibration run the week of Dec 14. Please confirm preferred times for the initial 72-hour soak and whether you want us to use your supplied traces (recommended) or our synthetic mix.

Attachments: SLA-matrix-vertex.xlsx; throughput-test-plan.pdf; kv-latency-samples.csv

If this looks good I’ll send the DocuSign exhibit and a short runbook for the soak.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Principal Sales Engineer 
Redwood Inference
